page: Microsoft Azure M128ms is an x86_64 memory-intensive server instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz, delivering 128 virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 3892.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 30.41 GB of RAM per physical core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 4194 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is limited, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests scoring in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core execution is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is a key strength, with uncached large-block read-only bandwidth reaching 375.19 GB/sec (top 10%) and write bandwidth at 150.99 GB/sec (top 25%).

Given its massive memory capacity and high memory bandwidth, the M128ms is highly resource-dense, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require large datasets to reside entirely in memory. It is well-suited for large-scale in-memory databases, as demonstrated by its strong Redis SET performance of 79.29 million operations per second, and high-throughput static web serving. However, due to its poor single-core performance and weak text generation speeds in LLM inference, it is not recommended for single-threaded tasks or real-time generative AI workloads.
